title: Proper counit is invertible on the distinguished open component
statement: For every M : DerivedCategory (pbcModules X (R.ring X)), the pullback along c.i of the proper derived counit for r.hom at the c.i-extension of M is an isomorphism.

source.place: Tags 0F7B and 0F7I, clopen restriction to the distinguished section.

proof_origin.place: Tags 0F7B and 0F7I, clopen distinguished-section calculation; implemented using the existing normalized ringed open exchange and reverse clopen adjunction.

from.place: Clopen distinguished-section calculation of the proper counit factor.

proof.text: Form W = c.Z ×[d.Z] X with projections g and p and section s = (c.i, id). The equations s ≫ g = c.i and s ≫ p = id make s open, and separatedness of the proper projection p makes s closed. Choose RW = g inverse(R.ring c.Z). Complete the given coefficient identifications along the two triangles using inverse-image composition; this supplies cs along s and cp along p, with a coherent ringed Cartesian square. No coherence assumption on R is added.

The open slice presentation and subterminality make the derived open-extension units for g and s invertible. The general identified-ring ordinaryClopenReverse lemma in IntegralRingedClopenComparison supplies pull(s) left adjoint to extension(s); exact localization gives the reverse derived adjunction. Uniqueness of left adjoints and pull(c.i) ≅ pull(g) ⋙ pull(s) identify pull(g) of the c.i-extension with extension(s).

The composite pull(p) ⋙ pull(s) is an equivalence: pullback composition identifies it with pullback along s ≫ p = id with an arbitrary coefficient isomorphism. The isomorphism-of-sites and scalar module equivalences prove that this identity pullback is an equivalence even when its coefficient isomorphism is not the canonical identity. The counit of the composite of the p-adjunction and the reverse s-adjunction is invertible. Its factorization, and full faithfulness of extension(s), imply invertibility of pull(s) applied to the p-counit at every s-extended object.

Apply open_comparison to the coherent ringed Cartesian square. Its derived mate is invertible. The mate-counit identity expresses the restriction along g of the r.hom-counit, composed with the invertible pullback-square comparison, as pull(p) of this mate followed by the p-counit. Apply pull(s), use the preceding supported-object calculation, cancel the comparison, and transport through pull(c.i) ≅ pull(g) ⋙ pull(s). This proves exactly the specified restricted r.hom-counit invertible. The categorical calculation is the proved private restrictionCounit lemma, with no remaining assumptions or holes.

lean.statement: theorem refinementProperCounit_isIso (M : DerivedCategory (pbcModules X (R.ring X))) : IsIso ((pull R c.i).map ((proEtaleRingDerivedAdjunction r.hom (R.ring d.Z) (R.ring c.Z) (R.pull r.hom)).counit.app ((openExtension R c.i).mapDerivedCategory.obj M)))
